Who advertises these data roles, how generic are the requirements, and what pay is shown?¶

Question. Who is advertising the data-role vacancies, how much requirement wording could fit almost any job, and what pay is shown?

Data. The local prepared primary-advert and requirement tables, with summary outputs from notebooks 02–04.

Method

  • Company careers ATS sources are direct by rule. On Reed and remote boards, a recruitment marker or local agency-name list indicates an agency.
  • Draw a seed-42 sample of 40 names from the weak no-marker bucket. Save names and one-by-one judgements locally.
  • Label generic soft-skill wording before checking for named tools or business areas. Exclude application text and clear company boilerplate.
  • Save the generic-sentence spot-check locally; notebook output contains counts only.
  • Keep row-level tables, advertiser names and advert sentences in local data folders. Page data contains aggregates only.

Generic relabel comparison. The retained pre-stage-8 result was 705 of 5,853 requirement sentences (12.0%), with a 10.5% median generic share per advert. The updated rules identify 939 of 5,840 requirement sentences as generic (16.1%), with a 15.4% median per advert. They check soft-skill cues before specific tools or business areas and exclude application or company-boilerplate text. Rory judged 4 of 15 concrete-labelled examples not concrete; the current generic share is best read as a lower bound. The earlier 46.9% / 44% figures cannot be reproduced from the retained outputs or pre-stage backup. Labels read “Codex judgement, human check pending”.

Who places the adverts?¶

A listed-by field is not populated in the prepared database, so the source and employer name are used. A company careers site on an applicant-tracking system (ATS) is direct by rule. On Reed and remote boards, recruitment terms or a reviewed agency name indicate an agency; other named employers are treated as direct.

The label file is an AI-made first pass. A person still needs to check it.

# Classify advertisers, review the top sixty names, and measure salary visibility.
import re
import unicodedata

ATS_SOURCES = {"greenhouse", "lever", "workable"}
EMPLOYER_SOURCES = {"reed", "remote_ok", "we_work_remotely"}
RECRUITING_WORDS = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:recruit\w*|resourcing|staffing|personnel|talent|search|selection|appointments)\b",
    flags=re.IGNORECASE,
)
METHOD_LABEL = "Codex judgement, human check pending"

def normalise_name(value) -> str:
    if pd.isna(value):
        return ""
    return " ".join(unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", str(value)).strip().casefold().split())

# The employer-name registry contains row-level names and stays in local data/labels.
agency_registry = pd.read_csv(LABELS / "agency_names.csv", dtype=str).fillna("")
MANUAL_AGENCY_ROOTS = {
    normalise_name(row.agency_name): str(row.reason)
    for row in agency_registry.itertuples(index=False)
    if normalise_name(row.agency_name)
}

def manual_agency_reason(name: str):
    for root, reason in MANUAL_AGENCY_ROOTS.items():
        if name == root or name.startswith(root + " ") or name.startswith(root + "-"):
            return reason
    return None

def assess_name(employer):
    name = normalise_name(employer)
    if not name or name in {"nan", "none", "unknown"}:
        return "unknown", "employer name missing", "No usable employer name is recorded."
    manual_reason = manual_agency_reason(name)
    if manual_reason:
        return "agency", "known agency name", manual_reason
    marker = RECRUITING_WORDS.search(name)
    if marker:
        return (
            "agency",
            "recruitment wording in employer name",
            f"Employer name contains the recruitment wording {marker.group(0)!r}.",
        )
    return (
        "direct_employer",
        "named employer without agency marker",
        "By-eye name review found no recruitment marker or known agency match.",
    )

def classify_advert(row):
    source = normalise_name(row["source"])
    if source in ATS_SOURCES:
        return "direct_employer", "company ATS source", "Company careers ATS sources are direct by rule."
    name_type, name_rule, reason = assess_name(row["employer"])
    if source in EMPLOYER_SOURCES:
        return name_type, name_rule, reason
    if name_type == "agency":
        return name_type, name_rule, reason
    return "unknown", "source not classified", "Source is outside the reviewed ATS, Reed and remote-board set."

classified = primary.apply(classify_advert, axis=1, result_type="expand")
classified.columns = ["advertiser_type", "advertiser_rule", "advertiser_reason"]
primary = pd.concat([primary.reset_index(drop=True), classified.reset_index(drop=True)], axis=1)

listed_by_empty = primary["listed_by"].isna() | primary["listed_by"].astype(str).str.strip().eq("")
add_finding("advertiser_listed_by_empty_primary", int(listed_by_empty.sum()), "Primary adverts with an empty listed-by field")

# Human-facing audit: each of the top sixty employer names receives a by-eye category and reason.
top60 = primary["employer"].fillna("").replace("", "<EMPTY>").value_counts().head(60)
top60_rows = []
for employer_name, advert_count in top60.items():
    name_type, name_rule, reason = assess_name(employer_name)
    top60_rows.append({
        "employer_name": employer_name,
        "advert_count": int(advert_count),
        "advertiser_type_by_name": name_type,
        "rule": name_rule,
        "reason": reason,
        "method": METHOD_LABEL,
    })
top60_review = pd.DataFrame(top60_rows)
top60_review.to_csv(LABELS / "employer_top60_review.csv", index=False)

agency_name_rows = {}
for employer_name in primary["employer"].dropna().drop_duplicates():
    name_type, name_rule, reason = assess_name(employer_name)
    if name_type == "agency":
        agency_name_rows[str(employer_name)] = {
            "agency_name": str(employer_name),
            "reason": reason,
        }
agency_names = pd.DataFrame(agency_name_rows.values()).sort_values("agency_name")
agency_names.to_csv(LABELS / "agency_names.csv", index=False)

advertiser_labels = primary[["vacancy_id", "advertiser_type", "advertiser_rule"]].rename(
    columns={"advertiser_rule": "rule"}
)
advertiser_labels["method"] = METHOD_LABEL
advertiser_labels.to_csv(LABELS / "advertiser_type.csv", index=False)

# Check the weak no-marker group, not the already rule-checked ATS/direct or agency labels.
name_check = pd.read_csv(LABELS / "advertiser_check.csv", dtype=str).fillna("")
weak_rule = "named employer without agency marker"
weak_bucket = primary.loc[primary["advertiser_rule"].eq(weak_rule)].copy()
expected_check_ids = set(
    weak_bucket.sort_values("vacancy_id").sample(n=40, random_state=SEED)["vacancy_id"].astype(str)
)
if len(name_check) != 40 or set(name_check["vacancy_id"].astype(str)) != expected_check_ids:
    raise ValueError("The local advertiser_check.csv file does not match the seed-42 sample of 40 weak-bucket labels.")
name_check["judgement"] = name_check["judgement"].str.casefold().str.strip()
name_check_counts = name_check["judgement"].value_counts()
flagged_count = int(name_check["judgement"].isin(["agency", "can't tell"]).sum())
name_check_rate = flagged_count / len(name_check)
reclassify_weak_bucket = name_check_rate > 0.10
primary["checked_advertiser_type"] = primary["advertiser_type"]
if reclassify_weak_bucket:
    primary.loc[primary["advertiser_rule"].eq(weak_rule), "checked_advertiser_type"] = "unclear"

print(f"Seed-42 sample from the weak no-marker bucket: {len(name_check)} labels.")
print("Sample judgements:", name_check_counts.to_dict())
print(f"Agency or can't tell: {flagged_count}/{len(name_check)} ({name_check_rate:.1%}); threshold is 10%.")
print(f"Reclassified the full weak bucket as unclear: {reclassify_weak_bucket} ({len(weak_bucket)} labels).")

print("listed_by empty:", f"{int(listed_by_empty.sum())} of {len(primary)} primary adverts")
print("Top-sixty employer review saved to data/labels/employer_top60_review.csv")
print("Top-sixty name labels:", top60_review["advertiser_type_by_name"].value_counts().to_dict())
print("Saved agency name rows:", len(agency_names))
print("Advertiser labels:", primary["advertiser_type"].value_counts().to_dict())

# Compare the current name heuristic with the seed-42 review and calculate salary visibility.
TYPE_ORDERS = {
    "current_name_rules": ["agency", "direct_employer", "unknown"],
    "after_seed42_review": ["agency", "direct_employer", "unclear"],
}
TYPE_COLUMNS = {
    "current_name_rules": "advertiser_type",
    "after_seed42_review": "checked_advertiser_type",
}
POOL_MASKS = {
    "data_role_pool": primary["data_role_pool_bool"],
    "shown": primary["is_shown_bool"],
}
primary["salary_hidden"] = ~pd.to_numeric(primary["salary_stated"], errors="coerce").eq(1)

type_share_rows = []
hidden_type_rows = []
for classification, column in TYPE_COLUMNS.items():
    type_order = TYPE_ORDERS[classification]
    for pool_name, pool_mask in POOL_MASKS.items():
        subset = primary.loc[pool_mask].copy()
        pool_n = len(subset)
        for advertiser_type in type_order:
            group = subset.loc[subset[column].eq(advertiser_type)]
            type_share_rows.append({
                "classification": classification, "pool": pool_name,
                "advertiser_type": advertiser_type, "adverts": len(group),
                "share": len(group) / pool_n if pool_n else np.nan,
            })
            hidden_type_rows.append({
                "classification": classification, "pool": pool_name,
                "advertiser_type": advertiser_type, "adverts": len(group),
                "salary_hidden": int(group["salary_hidden"].sum()),
                "share_salary_hidden": group["salary_hidden"].mean() if len(group) else np.nan,
            })
advertiser_type_shares = pd.DataFrame(type_share_rows)
hidden_pay_by_type = pd.DataFrame(hidden_type_rows)
advertiser_type_shares.to_csv(TABLES / "advertiser_type_shares.csv", index=False)
hidden_pay_by_type.to_csv(TABLES / "hidden_pay_by_advertiser.csv", index=False)

def source_family(source):
    source = normalise_name(source)
    if source in ATS_SOURCES: return "Company ATS boards"
    if source == "reed": return "Reed"
    return "Remote boards"

role_pool = primary.loc[primary["data_role_pool_bool"]].copy()
role_pool["source_family"] = role_pool["source"].map(source_family)
hidden_pay_by_source = role_pool.groupby("source_family", as_index=False).agg(
    adverts=("vacancy_id", "size"), salary_hidden=("salary_hidden", "sum"),
)
hidden_pay_by_source["share_salary_hidden"] = hidden_pay_by_source["salary_hidden"] / hidden_pay_by_source["adverts"]
hidden_pay_by_source.to_csv(TABLES / "hidden_pay_by_source.csv", index=False)

def salary_visibility_test(data, column, groups, classification, scope):
    table = pd.crosstab(data[column], data["salary_hidden"]).reindex(
        index=groups, columns=[False, True], fill_value=0
    )
    chi2, p_value, dof, expected = chi2_contingency(table.to_numpy(), correction=False)
    n = int(table.to_numpy().sum())
    result = {
        "classification": classification, "scope": scope,
        "test": "Pearson chi-square test of independence", "n": n,
        "chi_square": float(chi2), "degrees_of_freedom": int(dof),
        "p_value": float(p_value),
        "cramers_v": float(math.sqrt(chi2 / n)) if n else np.nan,
        "minimum_expected_count": float(expected.min()),
    }
    for group in groups:
        row = table.loc[group]
        total = int(row.sum())
        safe = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "_", group.casefold()).strip("_")
        result[f"{safe}_hidden"] = int(row[True])
        result[f"{safe}_total"] = total
        result[f"{safe}_share_hidden"] = float(row[True] / total) if total else np.nan
    return result

current_data_role = role_pool.copy()
current_reed = current_data_role.loc[current_data_role["source"].eq("reed")].copy()
checked_data_role = current_data_role.copy()
salary_tests = pd.DataFrame([
    salary_visibility_test(current_data_role, "advertiser_type", ["agency", "direct_employer"], "current_name_rules", "Data-role pool; two current name groups"),
    salary_visibility_test(current_reed, "advertiser_type", ["agency", "direct_employer"], "current_name_rules", "Reed only; two current name groups"),
    salary_visibility_test(checked_data_role, "checked_advertiser_type", ["agency", "direct_employer", "unclear"], "after_seed42_review", "Data-role pool; three checked groups"),
])
salary_tests.to_csv(TABLES / "advertiser_salary_tests.csv", index=False)

for metric, value, label in [
    ("advertiser_check_sample_size", len(name_check), "Seed-42 advertiser-name sample size"),
    ("advertiser_check_distinct_names", int(name_check["employer"].nunique()), "Distinct advertiser labels in the 40-advert sample"),
    ("advertiser_check_agency_count", int(name_check_counts.get("agency", 0)), "Sample names judged to be agencies"),
    ("advertiser_check_employer_count", int(name_check_counts.get("employer", 0)), "Sample names judged to be employers"),
    ("advertiser_check_unclear_count", int(name_check_counts.get("can't tell", 0)), "Sample names that could not be classified from the name"),
    ("advertiser_check_flagged_share", float(name_check_rate), "Sample share judged agency or unclear"),
    ("advertiser_check_agency_share", float(name_check_counts.get("agency", 0) / len(name_check)), "Sample share judged agency"),
]: add_finding(metric, value, label)

current_direct = hidden_pay_by_type.query("classification == 'current_name_rules' and pool == 'data_role_pool' and advertiser_type == 'direct_employer'").iloc[0]
current_agency = hidden_pay_by_type.query("classification == 'current_name_rules' and pool == 'data_role_pool' and advertiser_type == 'agency'").iloc[0]
checked_direct = hidden_pay_by_type.query("classification == 'after_seed42_review' and pool == 'data_role_pool' and advertiser_type == 'direct_employer'").iloc[0]
checked_agency = hidden_pay_by_type.query("classification == 'after_seed42_review' and pool == 'data_role_pool' and advertiser_type == 'agency'").iloc[0]
checked_unclear = hidden_pay_by_type.query("classification == 'after_seed42_review' and pool == 'data_role_pool' and advertiser_type == 'unclear'").iloc[0]
for metric, value, label in [
    ("salary_hidden_current_direct_share", float(current_direct["share_salary_hidden"]), "Hidden-salary share for current direct-name labels in the data-role pool"),
    ("salary_hidden_current_agency_share", float(current_agency["share_salary_hidden"]), "Hidden-salary share for agency labels in the data-role pool"),
    ("salary_hidden_reviewed_direct_share", float(checked_direct["share_salary_hidden"]), "Hidden-salary share for ATS direct labels after the name check"),
    ("salary_hidden_reviewed_agency_share", float(checked_agency["share_salary_hidden"]), "Hidden-salary share for agency labels after the name check"),
    ("salary_hidden_reviewed_unclear_share", float(checked_unclear["share_salary_hidden"]), "Hidden-salary share for unclear labels after the name check"),
]: add_finding(metric, value, label)

print("Current name-rule shares and the post-sample three-group shares:")
display(advertiser_type_shares)
print("Hidden-pay shares by group; the reviewed version keeps the uncertain bucket visible:")
display(hidden_pay_by_type)
print("The three-group chi-square applies to the data-role pool. Reed-only direct comparison is retained for the original labels; after review, Reed has no direct-labelled rows because its no-marker names are unclear.")
display(salary_tests)

# A2: label one distinct sentence per requirement ID; remove non-requirements first.
sentence_rows = requirements.loc[requirements["vacancy_id"].isin(set(full_data_role["vacancy_id"]))].copy()
sentence_rows = sentence_rows.drop_duplicates("req_id", keep="first").copy()
sentence_rows["evidence_sentence"] = sentence_rows["evidence_sentence"].fillna("").astype(str).str.replace(r"\s+", " ", regex=True).str.strip()

NON_REQUIREMENT_RE = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:this is a beta feature to avoid spam applicants|advert closing date|how to apply|application process|"
    r"to apply\s*:|please submit (?:a )?(?:resume|cv|cover letter)|please apply with .*\b(?:cv|resume)|"
    r"if you are interested .*\bplease apply|reasonable accommodation for any part of the application process|"
    r"(?:we have|our)\s+(?:a\s+)?(?:dynamic|diverse|international)\b.{0,120}\b(?:customer|client) base\b|"
    r"equal opportunities? employer|equal opportunity employer)\b", re.IGNORECASE
)
GENERIC_PHRASES = [
    ("communication as a general soft skill", r"\b(?:communication|communicate)(?: skills?)?\b"),
    ("team player, teamwork or team spirit", r"\b(?:team player|teamwork|team spirit|work well in a team|work as part of a team)\b"),
    ("collaboration as a soft skill", r"\bcollaborat\w*\b"),
    ("attention to detail", r"\battention to detail\b|\bdetail[- ]oriented\b"),
    ("analytical skills in general terms", r"\banalytical (?:skills?|mindset|thinking|ability|abilities)\b"),
    ("strategic thinking as a broad personal quality", r"\bstrategic thinking\b"),
    ("product taste as a subjective personal quality", r"\bproduct taste\b"),
    ("self-motivation", r"\bself[- ]motivated\b|\bself[- ]starter\b"),
    ("fast-paced environment", r"\bfast[- ]paced\b"),
    ("adaptability", r"\badaptable\b|\badaptability\b"),
    ("solutions-focused wording", r"\bsolutions?[- ]focused\b"),
    ("passion or enthusiasm", r"\bpassion(?:ate)?\b|\benthusiastic\b"),
    ("ability to multitask", r"\bmultitask(?:ing)?\b|\bmulti[- ]task(?:ing)?\b"),
    ("drive as a personal quality", r"\b(?:bringing|bring|have|having|possess|demonstrate)\s+(?:a\s+)?(?:strong\s+)?drive\b|,\s*drive\s*,|\bdrive\s+and\s+(?:team spirit|initiative)\b"),
    ("stock wording about confidence or motivation", r"\b(?:self-confident|driven individual|motivated individual|positive attitude|strong work ethic)\b"),
    ("general work environment wording", r"\b(?:fun and intense|fun environment|positive work environment)\b"),
    ("fluency or general language ability", r"\b(?:fluent|fluency) in English\b|\bwritten and spoken English\b"),
    ("working under pressure", r"\bwork(?:ing)? under pressure\b"),
    ("organisation or time management", r"\b(?:highly )?organi[sz]ed\b|\btime management\b"),
    ("problem-solving as a general trait", r"\bproblem[- ]solving skills?\b"),
    ("interpersonal skills", r"\binterpersonal skills?\b"),
]
GENERIC_RE = [(label, re.compile(pattern, re.IGNORECASE)) for label, pattern in GENERIC_PHRASES]
TOOL_RE = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:sql|excel|python|pandas|r|tableau|power\s*bi|looker|snowflake|dbt|dax|html|css|erp|kubernetes|rabbitmq|kafka|figma|webflow|mongodb|mysql|postgresql|oracle|sap|"
    r"databricks|azure|aws|gcp|google analytics|ga4|salesforce|hubspot|jira|microsoft copilot|copilot|ci/cd|continuous integration|continuous delivery|"
    r"power\s*query|power\s*pivot|vba|sas|spss|qlik|bigquery|redshift)\b", re.IGNORECASE
)
OUTPUT_RE = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:dashboard\w*|report\w*|dataset\w*|data set\w*|database\w*|query|queries|pipeline\w*|etl|visuali[sz]ation\w*|forecast\w*|"
    r"data quality|data validation|data cleaning|business intelligence|data model\w*|model\w*|kpi\w*|metric\w*|spreadsheet\w*|workbook\w*|"
    r"pricing|budget\w*|inventory|supply chain|customer analytics|financial analysis|sales analysis|marketing analytics|product analytics|"
    r"job grading outcomes?|clinical trials?|clinical data management|contract management systems?|fund accounting|private equity|hedge fund taxation|"
    r"market intelligence|commodit(?:y|ies)(?: data| trade flows)?|air monitoring|leak testing|entity resolution|external feed ingestion|integration architecture|"
    r"semantic modell?ing|data engineering|customer relationships?|account structure|campaign planning|data-informed decision-making|reliability|observability|supportability)\b", re.IGNORECASE
)
BUSINESS_AREA_RE = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:finance|financial|sales|marketing|operations|risk|human resources|hr|product|pricing|insurance|manufacturing|logistics|commercial|retail|"
    r"healthcare|supply chain|customer service|customer insight|banking|payments|procurement|education|energy|clinical|accounting|taxation|equity|commodities|"
    r"market intelligence|data engineering|technical account management|economics|computer science|statistics|quantitative field|scientific discipline|degree in)\b", re.IGNORECASE
)
TASK_VERB_RE = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:build\w*|creat\w*|develop\w*|design\w*|produc\w*|deliver\w*|analys\w*|analyz\w*|lead|led|driv\w*|own\w*|support\w*|"
    r"implement\w*|collat\w*|translat\w*|carry out|operat\w*|manag\w*|coordinat\w*|ship\w*|ingest\w*|stream\w*|resolv\w*|test\w*|"
    r"monitor\w*|configur\w*|maintain\w*|validat\w*|forecast\w*|model\w*|quer\w*|clean\w*|transform\w*|reconcil\w*|automat\w*|"
    r"visuali[sz]\w*|report\w*|extract\w*|investigat\w*|measur\w*|calculat\w*|present\w*|map\w*|segment\w*|audit\w*|integrat\w*|"
    r"track\w*|evaluat\w*|prioriti[sz]\w*|plan\w*|write\w*|deploy\w*|troubleshoot\w*)\b", re.IGNORECASE
)

def label_sentence(sentence):
    text = " ".join(str(sentence).split())
    if NON_REQUIREMENT_RE.search(text):
        return "excluded", "rule: non-requirement", "Application instructions or advert boilerplate; not a candidate requirement."
    generic_match = next(((label, pattern.search(text)) for label, pattern in GENERIC_RE if pattern.search(text)), None)
    if generic_match:
        cue, match = generic_match
        return "generic", "rule: soft-skill or stock wording", f"Broad wording about {cue}; a named team or business area does not make it task-specific."
    tool = TOOL_RE.search(text)
    if tool:
        return "concrete", "rule: named tool", f"Names a specific tool or platform: {tool.group(0)}."
    for pattern, basis in ((OUTPUT_RE, "rule: named task or output"), (BUSINESS_AREA_RE, "rule: named business area")):
        match = pattern.search(text)
        if match:
            return "concrete", basis, f"Names a task, output or business area: {match.group(0)}."
    if TASK_VERB_RE.search(text) and len(text.split()) >= 5:
        return "concrete", "Codex judgement", "Names a role-specific work task without a named tool."
    if re.search(r"\b(?:skill|skills|ability|abilities|knowledge|understanding|experience|expertise|motivated|driven|reliable|confident)\b", text, re.IGNORECASE):
        return "generic", "Codex judgement", "Describes a broad personal quality or capability without a specific task."
    return "concrete", "Codex judgement", "Describes a role-specific subject, responsibility or work context."

sentence_labels = sentence_rows["evidence_sentence"].map(label_sentence)
sentence_rows[["label", "basis", "reason"]] = pd.DataFrame(sentence_labels.tolist(), index=sentence_rows.index)
sentence_rows["reason"] = sentence_rows["reason"].str.replace(r"\s+", " ", regex=True).str.strip()
sentence_rows["method"] = "Codex judgement, human check pending"
sentence_label_output = sentence_rows[
    ["req_id", "vacancy_id", "label", "basis", "reason", "method", "evidence_sentence"]
].copy()
sentence_label_output.to_csv(LABELS / "sentence_generic.csv", index=False)

print("Non-requirement sentences excluded:", int(sentence_label_output["label"].eq("excluded").sum()))
print("Classified requirement sentences:", sentence_label_output["label"].isin(["generic", "concrete"]).sum())
label_counts = sentence_label_output["label"].value_counts().rename_axis("label").reset_index(name="sentence_occurrences")
display(label_counts)

How much requirement wording is generic?¶

Generic phrases include communication, teamwork, collaboration, attention to detail, general analytical ability, self-motivation, fast-paced work, adaptability, solutions-focused wording, passion and multitasking. These stay generic even when a team or business area is named. Application instructions and clear company boilerplate are excluded. The labels are Codex judgement, human check pending.

Rory judged 4 of 15 examples labelled concrete as generic or not requirements at all. Treat the current generic share as a lower bound; the full spot-check rows remain local.

# Calculate per-advert shares and compare the requested groups.
scope_ads = full_data_role[[
    "vacancy_id", "outcome", "is_shown_bool", "employer", "source"
]].copy().merge(
    primary[["vacancy_id", "checked_advertiser_type"]].drop_duplicates("vacancy_id"),
    on="vacancy_id",
    how="left",
)
included_sentence_labels = sentence_label_output.loc[sentence_label_output["label"].isin(["generic", "concrete"])].copy()
sentence_counts = included_sentence_labels.groupby("vacancy_id").agg(
    sentence_count=("req_id", "nunique"),
    generic_count=("label", lambda values: int(values.eq("generic").sum())),
).reset_index()
per_advert = scope_ads.merge(sentence_counts, on="vacancy_id", how="left")
per_advert[["sentence_count", "generic_count"]] = per_advert[["sentence_count", "generic_count"]].fillna(0)
per_advert["generic_share"] = np.where(
    per_advert["sentence_count"].gt(0),
    per_advert["generic_count"] / per_advert["sentence_count"],
    np.nan,
)
per_advert["generic_percent"] = per_advert["generic_share"] * 100
eligible_per_ad = per_advert.loc[per_advert["generic_share"].notna()].copy()

sentence_summary = (
    included_sentence_labels["label"].value_counts()
    .reindex(["generic", "concrete"], fill_value=0)
    .rename_axis("label")
    .reset_index(name="sentences")
)
sentence_summary["share"] = sentence_summary["sentences"] / sentence_summary["sentences"].sum()
sentence_summary.to_csv(TABLES / "generic_sentence_summary.csv", index=False)

bin_edges = np.linspace(0, 1, 11)
bin_labels = [f"{int(a*100)}–{int(b*100)}%" for a, b in zip(bin_edges[:-1], bin_edges[1:])]
eligible_per_ad["share_band"] = pd.cut(
    eligible_per_ad["generic_share"],
    bins=bin_edges,
    labels=bin_labels,
    include_lowest=True,
    right=True,
)
generic_distribution = (
    eligible_per_ad["share_band"].value_counts(sort=False)
    .rename_axis("generic_share_band")

)
generic_distribution["share_of_adverts"] = generic_distribution["adverts"] / len(eligible_per_ad)
generic_distribution.to_csv(TABLES / "generic_share_distribution.csv", index=False)

def compare_generic_share(group_one, group_two, label_one, label_two):
    x = group_one["generic_share"].dropna().to_numpy()
    y = group_two["generic_share"].dropna().to_numpy()
    test = mannwhitneyu(x, y, alternative="two-sided", method="auto")
    n_product = len(x) * len(y)
    return {
        "comparison": f"{label_one} vs {label_two}",
        "group_one": label_one,
        "group_two": label_two,
        "n_one": len(x),
        "n_two": len(y),
        "median_one": float(np.median(x)) if len(x) else np.nan,
        "median_two": float(np.median(y)) if len(y) else np.nan,
        "mann_whitney_u": float(test.statistic),
        "p_value": float(test.pvalue),
        "rank_biserial": float(2 * test.statistic / n_product - 1) if n_product else np.nan,
        "test": "Two-sided Mann–Whitney U; compares independent advert-level shares",
    }

shown_ads = eligible_per_ad.loc[eligible_per_ad["is_shown_bool"]]
senior_ads = eligible_per_ad.loc[eligible_per_ad["outcome"].astype(str).str.casefold().eq("senior role")]
agency_ads = eligible_per_ad.loc[eligible_per_ad["checked_advertiser_type"].eq("agency")]
direct_ads = eligible_per_ad.loc[eligible_per_ad["checked_advertiser_type"].eq("direct_employer")]
unclear_ads = eligible_per_ad.loc[eligible_per_ad["checked_advertiser_type"].eq("unclear")]
generic_comparisons = pd.DataFrame([
    compare_generic_share(shown_ads, senior_ads, "shown", "senior"),
    compare_generic_share(agency_ads, direct_ads, "agency", "direct employer (reviewed)"),
    compare_generic_share(agency_ads, unclear_ads, "agency", "unclear (reviewed)"),
    compare_generic_share(direct_ads, unclear_ads, "direct employer (reviewed)", "unclear (reviewed)"),
])

    for label, group in [("Agency", agency_ads), ("Direct employer (reviewed)", direct_ads), ("Unclear", unclear_ads)]
])
generic_advertiser_summary.to_csv(TABLES / "generic_share_by_advertiser.csv", index=False)

The sentence chart shows the overall split and how the generic share varies from advert to advert. The Mann–Whitney tests compare independent advert-level shares; they do not assume those shares follow a normal distribution. Full sentence labels and reasons are saved locally in data/labels/sentence_generic.csv; the 15-per-label spot-check is saved in data/labels/sentence_generic_spotcheck.csv. The saved notebook outputs show counts only.

            "essential": essential,

            "share_essential": essential / len(vacancy_ids) if vacancy_ids else 0.0,
        }
    skill_records.append(record)

# Build the three page chart data files from summary findings only.
def existing_value(item_id):
    match = next((item for item in findings if item.get("id") == item_id), None)
    if match is None:
        raise KeyError(f"Missing source finding: {item_id}")
    return match["value"]

    ("All primary adverts", int(existing_value("anchor_primary_adverts"))),
    ("Data-role pool", int(existing_value("anchor_data_role_pool"))),
    ("Local roles before seniority", int(funnel_lookup["After excluding overseas-only remote adverts"])),
    ("After seniority", int(funnel_lookup["After excluding senior roles"])),
    ("Shown to a graduate", int(existing_value("anchor_shown_adverts"))),
]
for step_id, value in [
    ("funnel_local_before_seniority", funnel_specs[2][1]),

    ("funnel_after_professional_qualification", int(funnel_lookup["After excluding professional-qualification roles"])),
    ("funnel_shown_after_location_filter", funnel_specs[4][1]),
]:
    add_finding(step_id, value, step_id.replace("_", " ").capitalize())
funnel_page_data = {
    "total_dots": int(existing_value("anchor_primary_adverts")),

    "steps": [{"label": label, "count": count} for label, count in funnel_specs],
}
(PAGE_DATA / "funnel_steps.json").write_text(json.dumps(funnel_page_data, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")

# Summary-only notebook figures; advert names and rows remain in local data folders.
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 5.4), gridspec_kw={"width_ratios": [1.15, 1.3]})
reviewed = advertiser_type_shares.loc[
    advertiser_type_shares["classification"].eq("after_seed42_review")
]
colors = {"agency": "#2b3a55", "direct_employer": "#3d5a80", "unclear": "#98c1d9"}
for y, pool_name in enumerate(["data_role_pool", "shown"]):
    rows = reviewed.loc[reviewed["pool"].eq(pool_name)].set_index("advertiser_type")
    left = 0.0
    for kind in TYPE_ORDERS["after_seed42_review"]:
        share = float(rows.loc[kind, "share"])
        axes[0].barh(y, share, left=left, color=colors[kind], height=0.58, label=kind.replace("_", " "))
        if share >= 0.07:
            axes[0].text(left + share / 2, y, f"{share:.1%}", ha="center", va="center", color="white" if kind != "unclear" else "#161616", fontsize=10, weight="bold")
        left += share
axes[0].set_yticks([0, 1], ["Data-role pool", "Shown adverts"])
axes[0].set_xlim(0, 1)
axes[0].set_xlabel("Share of adverts")
axes[0].set_title("After the weak name bucket moves to unclear")
axes[0].legend(frameon=False, loc="lower center", bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.36), ncol=3)

bar_rows = []
for classification, title in [("current_name_rules", "Current name rules"), ("after_seed42_review", "After sample review")]:
    rows = hidden_pay_by_type.query("classification == @classification and pool == 'data_role_pool'")
    for row in rows.itertuples(index=False):
        if row.adverts:
            bar_rows.append({"label": f"{title}: {row.advertiser_type.replace('_', ' ')}", "share": row.share_salary_hidden, "hidden": row.salary_hidden, "n": row.adverts})
plot_df = pd.DataFrame(bar_rows)
bars = axes[1].barh(plot_df["label"], plot_df["share"], color=["#2b3a55" if "agency" in label else "#3d5a80" if "direct" in label else "#98c1d9" for label in plot_df["label"]], height=0.65)
for bar, row in zip(bars, plot_df.itertuples(index=False)):
    axes[1].text(bar.get_width() + 0.012, bar.get_y() + bar.get_height()/2, f"{row.hidden}/{row.n} · {row.share:.1%}", va="center", fontsize=9)
axes[1].set_xlim(0, min(1.0, max(float(plot_df["share"].max()) * 1.42, 0.15)))
axes[1].xaxis.set_major_formatter(PercentFormatter(1))
axes[1].set_xlabel("Share with no salary stated")
axes[1].set_title("Direct-labelled adverts still hide pay more often")
for ax in axes:
    ax.grid(axis="x", color="#e2ded5", linewidth=0.8)
    ax.set_axisbelow(True)
    ax.spines[["top", "right", "left"]].set_visible(False)
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig(FIGURES / "05_advertisers_and_hidden_pay.png", dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight")
plt.close(fig)
display(Image(filename=str(FIGURES / "05_advertisers_and_hidden_pay.png")))

The name-only labels initially treated every no-marker name as direct. The 40-name check found many agencies and uncertain names in that bucket. The reviewed chart moves the whole weak bucket to “unclear”, leaving company ATS listings in “direct”. Agency and direct-labelled groups still differ in how often salary is missing; the chart shows association, not cause.

def json_records(path):
    frame = pd.read_csv(path, low_memory=False)
    return json.loads(frame.to_json(orient="records", double_precision=8))

def make_table(csv_name, columns):
    return {
        "columns": [{"key": key, "label": label} for key, label in columns],
        "rows": json_records(PAGE_DATA / csv_name),
        "download": csv_name,
    }

What this shows¶

The advertiser shares describe who places the captured listings, not who wrote the wording. The salary tests show sample associations; source mix matters because company ATS adverts are direct by rule. The generic-sentence results are based on one labelled occurrence per requirement ID, with one advert-level share for each full description. The shown-ad pay band uses annualised midpoints and also preserves the widest annualised salary bounds.

Limits¶

  • Captured listings are not a census of the job market.
  • Employer-name, AI and genericity labels say “Codex judgement, human check pending”; a person has not checked all labels.
  • The full-description sentence analysis excludes adverts with search excerpts only.
  • Salary is missing from some shown adverts, and the displayed band describes adverts, not what people are paid.
  • The page data contains aggregate counts only. It has no vacancy IDs, advert titles, employer names or requirement sentences.
